newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tractebel declines comment on Mestrallet.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel declines comment on Mestrallet.

text.p: Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA on Monday declined to comment on the position of Gerard Mestrallet, the French chairman of its board.
In an interview with Belgian daily La Libre Belgique on Saturday, Jean-Louis Duplat, head of the regulatory Banking and Finance Commission (BFC), questioned Mestrallet's position.
"If we are going towards a corporate governance type similar to that of the banking industry, the chairman can never be a representative of the leading shareholder," La Libre quoted him as saying.
Mestrallet is head of French Compagnie de Suez, which controls Tractebel via its Belgian unit Societe Generale de Belgique.
The planned merger of Suez with French utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux has led to worries in Belgium that Tractebel's expansion would be stifled.
Flemish Economics Minister Eric Van Rompuy last month also criticised Mestrallet's position in Tractebel.
In response to political worries about French dominance of Tractebel, Tractebel is currently in the process of adapting its statutes in order to become a so-called autonomous company.
This will be done partly through the nomination of a series of independent board members at Tractebel.
Similar statutory provisions already exist in the Belgian banking industry.
